title: Standardize collaboration terminology across every interface
author: w0F5vYijNonu8kkqLSa_jYY4GIV-Q5HpbxYY525ggm4

events.title: Standardize collaboration terminology across every interface
events.body:
## Outcome

Use familiar Git and review terms consistently in browser, desktop, mobile, command-line, API, diagnostics, and generated documentation.

## Implementation

- Adopt Pull request, Review, Branch, Fork, Source node, Mirror, Seed, Pin, Verified mirror, and Trusted maintainer as the user-facing vocabulary.
- Reserve patch for an actual textual or binary patch or patchset, never the pull-request object itself.
- Keep backward-compatible internal aliases and migration readers without exposing legacy terms in new UI.
- Create a source scanner with a narrow technical allowlist for protocol field names and historical records.
- Update accessibility names, empty states, errors, commands, API descriptions, and localization keys together.

## Acceptance criteria

- The terminology scan passes across all current user-facing surfaces.
- Existing stored records and external API clients continue to load through aliases.
- No error path or offline state reintroduces a retired term.
- Screen-reader labels and visible labels describe the same object.
- Generated capability and protocol documentation uses the canonical glossary.

## Dependencies

Defines the vocabulary contract consumed by every other sprint issue.

## Verification

Run the source scanner, legacy-record migrations, API compatibility fixtures, screenshots, accessibility snapshots, and representative online and offline error paths.
